issues.problem: Every accepted candidate span is projected into one Checkpoint without a gate for an evaluable management question, a concrete action space, or the clinician protocol's primary preoperative-path/NAT-reassessment task. Admission intent, generic wording, repeats, execution traces, postoperative routine care and intraoperative records can therefore become apparent standalone evaluation points even when a clinician cannot supply a valid next action.
issues.implementation: candidate_checkpoints.py adds source-level grouping, support/out-of-scope/review migrations, concrete action-plan schema and management clock gates. candidate_materials.py adds timed projections. SCALE-01 candidate-cp-v4 retains five management CPs; the admission-intent and two clockless candidates are not CPs. Real discovery recall remains under separate validation.

real_counterexample.quote: 为求手术治疗，门诊以"胰腺癌"收入我科。
real_counterexample.counts: 38 candidate spans produced 38 candidate materials; record_function counts were new_decision=24, reassessment=2, execution=6, repeat=3, generic=2, uncertain=1. Nine postoperative-course, three discharge-summary and two operative candidates were also in the same pool.

issues.synthetic_counterexample: A located admission-intent sentence and a generic template remain auditable source records but cannot become standalone evaluable Checkpoints. A documented plan with a patient-specific question and ADVANCE/HOLD_FOR_EVIDENCE/REDIRECT action space can.
issues.positive_control: An evaluation unit has one explicit task header, patient-specific available facts and a concrete action space; maintaining a strategy after new evidence is allowed and does not require a changed Mode.
issues.negative_control: repeat, execution, generic and uncertain spans do not become independent scored Checkpoints merely because their quotes verify. Postoperative treatment, acute complications and intraoperative resection/reconstruction are not silently included in the primary preoperative task.
planned_test_contracts: The admission-intent real quote is retained for audit but is not independently evaluable.
A missing action plan is a technical failure, not a valid blank Checkpoint.
Primary-task exclusion is distinct from patient exclusion and from source deletion.
Every retained unit can emit a concrete action plan under the frozen clinician form.
issues.limitations: Offline eligibility and migration are implemented and audited. This is not an expert-labelled exclusion set or clinical accuracy result; real discovery recall and clinical task semantics remain pending.

issues.problem: Multiple candidates from one source become separate Checkpoints, while masking removes only the current span and strictly later spans. Same-source/same-clock alternatives remain visible in both directions, and earlier decisions remain visible in later packets, causing duplication and cross-Checkpoint target leakage.
issues.implementation: candidate_checkpoints.py merges same-source spans with migration conservation. candidate_materials.py jointly masks member spans, same_event restatements and bounded adjacent action clauses in one original-text coordinate pass. Independent audits caught and verified repair of same-source leakage, over-masking and offset corruption. Cross-document completeness remains explicitly unconfirmed; output is not a doctor packet.

real_counterexample.observation: 38 Checkpoints came from 17 sources; 13 sources carried 34 Checkpoints. The preoperative-discussion source 4bf1aba342d3908a8d434716 carried five and the preoperative-summary source 52a8cea2c9edd711a4070c3d carried four.
real_counterexample.mechanism: materials._future_source_spans uses candidate clock strictly greater than target clock; project_materials adds only the current target span. Same-source same-clock candidates are not jointly masked.

issues.synthetic_counterexample: Combined, component and repeated action spans in one source must be one evaluation unit with one jointly masked target region set and a multi-action response, not separately navigable packets that reveal one another.
issues.positive_control: At most one evaluation Checkpoint is emitted per source in this iteration; all target decisions, cross-document restatements, post-decision execution and outcomes required by the frozen protocol are jointly masked without editing original sources.
issues.negative_control: No retained packet exposes another candidate from its own target source as an answer clue. Combining actions does not fabricate separate decision times or merge genuinely different source documents.
planned_test_contracts: The five-span preoperative-discussion source yields at most one evaluation unit and none of its five target quotes remains visible.
Combined and atomic spans are deduplicated/clustered with an auditable member-ID mapping rather than silently deleted.
Cross-document restatement and outcome leakage receive explicit mask coverage tests.
The old independent-span masking control HPL028 is migrated to distinguish raw discovery span retention from final evaluation-unit masking.
issues.limitations: One source one management CP is implemented in the offline projection. It is not a confirmed clinical decision time. Heuristic adjacent-action and cross-document masks remain a private development projection, not a frozen clinician blinding protocol.

issues.problem: Performed-test reports are indexed as evidence artifacts but the current pipeline has no evidence-arrival re-evaluation unit and no evidence_used edges were recorded. Consequently MR/contrast CT evidence cannot become a protocol-defined opportunity to maintain or change management. This general mechanism gap must not be misreported as a confirmed preoperative omission in SCALE-01: its selected report-visibility clocks are after the operation date, and no laparoscopy deployment was found in the delivered sources.
issues.implementation: diagnostic_events.py preserves exam/report/verified clocks, prefers report_time with verified fallback and derives an explicit operation-start boundary from an exact source field. candidate_checkpoints.py generates pre-exam and evidence-arrival candidates only with clocks, visible context and primary-task eligibility. SCALE-01 candidate-cp-v4 has MR/CT pre-exam and two preoperative report-arrival CPs; postoperative diagnostic nodes and the empty-context pre-exam node are excluded with migrations.

real_counterexample.MR: Three duplicate-content sources form EA-703970e18141230e: exam 2022-12-14 12:17:25, report 2022-12-14 14:56:32, selected verified-time proxy 2022-12-16 15:33:07.
real_counterexample.contrast_CT: Four duplicate-content sources form EA-674c217d0aad511b: exam 2022-12-14 14:31:11, report 2022-12-15 15:55:12, selected verified-time proxy 2022-12-18 19:05:11.
real_counterexample.laparoscopy: No 腹腔镜/腔镜探查/分期探查 occurrence was found in the 688-source SCALE-01 bundle; other cases still require a separate recall audit.

issues.synthetic_counterexample: A newly visible preoperative MR report creates an evidence-arrival re-evaluation opportunity linked to the current management question; the clinician may maintain or change the strategy. A report alone does not create a fictional clinician order or claim a documented new decision.
issues.positive_control: A patient-specific documented order for MR, contrast CT or staging laparoscopy remains discoverable as a management action; evidence arrival preserves exam/report/verified clocks and uses an explicit visibility policy.
issues.negative_control: A generic template suggestion, a report mention, or a postoperatively visible report is not fabricated into a preoperative management decision. Absence in SCALE-01 is not generalized to all cases.
planned_test_contracts: A preoperative visible evidence artifact can create a clearly labelled evidence-arrival re-evaluation candidate with an actionable Mode set.
SCALE-01 MR/CT artifacts do not enter the preoperative primary task under their selected verified-time visibility clocks.
Exam, report and verified timestamps remain distinct and the selected visibility basis is displayed.
A documented staging-laparoscopy order is discovered; a mere template/report mention is not promoted to a deployment.
Evidence_used and evidence_arrival are different relations; neither is inferred from timestamp or content similarity alone.
issues.limitations: Report_time and verified_time are source metadata, not independently validated clinician availability. Operation-boundary extraction is an explicit candidate requiring review, not complete treatment-stage reconstruction. Cross-case order recall, laparoscopy positive controls and clinician blinding remain open; no recall rate is claimed.

issues.problem: In SCALE-01 relations-r6-materials-v2, the current candidate was identified only by a hash, record_function and retrieval clock. The LLM-proposed located span was not shown, all sources were mixed under one 'complete materials' heading, and selecting an Episode left every candidate vertically stacked. The viewer could not directly inspect adjacent candidates or the Agent's relation evidence. Unknown-clock sources also printed None instead of their available source clocks.
issues.real_counterexample: SCALE-01 EP002 CP-59c0c3c3a267632a: the screenshot shows only the hash and 154 included sources, not the candidate's original span or its two same-Episode neighbors. The two unknown-clock neighbors show 'None'. This is a display/material-organization defect, not a clinical judgment about this candidate.
issues.synthetic_counterexample: A current candidate, a later same-process candidate and an unknown-clock candidate must expose separate researcher-only original spans, masked target sources, explicit retrieval-time roles, previous/next links, relation explanations and source creation-time clues. A doctor packet must not inherit these researcher originals or later packets.
issues.positive_control: One current candidate is displayed at a time; its source title and candidate quote are explicit; adjacent candidates and related-candidate links navigate; response exports bind checkpoint, packet hash, form version and manifest hash.
issues.negative_control: The masked target text must not contain the current candidate quote; unknown clocks must not claim completed masking; candidate display order must not be labelled clinical order; renderer/response must not create a clinical Reference.
issues.implementation: Material format 0.2.0 adds researcher_candidate_inspection, target source/time metadata, typed masked-source roles, related_candidates, and explicit candidate navigation. A local text-only HTML CLI renders one candidate at a time with layered source, relation and evidence panels and no network. A new versioned output directory preserves v2.
issues.limitations: Improved research inspection does not validate Agent candidate semantics, clinical Episode independence, actual evidence use, or blinding completeness. The HTML is a private research preview, not a doctor release. The frozen clinician protocol and separate per-assignment package remain unimplemented.

issues.problem: The selected execution scope was accidentally placed in the fixed AUTH_REQUIRED dictionary with the legacy value. It made a correctly bound discovery authorization fail the fixed-value governance check before any provider call; a boolean can also compare equal to a string under a generic equality check if the field is not explicitly typed.
issues.synthetic_counterexample: A discovery contract with a matching discovery scope and an old legacy AUTH_REQUIRED entry must be rejected by the implementation defect, then accepted after removing that fixed entry and checking the contract-bound scope as a string.
issues.positive_control: A discovery authorization with the exact selected scope and current code/source/config hashes validates.
issues.negative_control: The legacy scope or boolean true does not validate against a discovery contract.
issues.real_run_note: SCALE-01 discovery-r1 preflight failed before provider construction on the first attempts; the log was a preflight failure, not a patient or model result. The authorization was then rebound after this correction.

issues.problem: Ordering could not see program evidence artifacts, context_only had the same process-union effect as supported, and contains/overlap lacked an object model. Replacing ordering's name alone would not repair those contracts.
issues.synthetic_counterexample: An earlier evidence artifact must be visible beside a later management candidate; a reversed or temporally later evidence relation must be refused; context_only and contains/overlap must preserve separate process containers.
issues.positive_control: A supported evidence_used edge from an earlier artifact to a later management expression is preserved as a directed reference without process union; a supported process relation merges.
issues.negative_control: Evidence cannot be a same_event/same_management_process endpoint; an artifact cannot be reversed as the later management endpoint; unsupported process links do not merge.
issues.development_counterexample: The first shared-builder implementation applied supported_only without an explicit policy. That also changed legacy ordering + episodes to stop merging context_only, contrary to the agreed unchanged baseline. HCO006 now proves the default legacy merge directly; the new case path opts into supported_only explicitly.
issues.core_task_refinement_2026_11_13: Per the user's development principle, case organization is now edges-only: no agent preview, demotion, episode-coverage checklist, or separate evidence-check list. Program code derives containers after edges are recorded. HCO009 verifies the reduced tool surface; HCO007 verifies recovery still preserves relations. A separate organization entry binds and reads a frozen discovery result without rerunning discovery (HRC015/HRN006).
issues.limitations: The legacy ordering + episodes path remains available for comparison. It retains historical context_only merging so old counterexamples can be replayed as the legacy baseline. The new path only unions supported process edges. Program quote and clock gates do not establish clinical correctness; a single model organization run still requires source-based review. Checkpoint material organization and frozen blinding are not implemented by this change.

issues.problem: In SCALE-01 relations-r1, billed format-repair requests were not preceded by durable session records of their repair prompt. The transcript had request_sent(repair=true) but could not reconstruct the exact provider input.
issues.implementation: Repair context is appended to the session before the repair request and the actual request reads derive_messages(). No synthetic tool result is fabricated; oversized-prefix receipts remain explicit user messages.

issues.problem: SpillStore instructed the model to call read_spilled, but Harness.new_registry never registered that tool. The first oversized list_events result therefore led to UNKNOWN_TOOL instead of readable evidence.
issues.real_counterexample: SCALE-01 relations-r1 seq 16 called read_spilled and seq 17 returned UNKNOWN_TOOL.
issues.implementation: Every Harness registry now includes a read_spilled reader restricted to that run's spill directory.

issues.problem: max_steps_per_turn=14 counted the entire case-level list/read/record/finish task, and STOP_MAX_TURNS made step exhaustion look like a turn cap. In SCALE-01 relations-r1 the model read all 43 nodes and multiple original spans, but exhausted the cap before record_relation; zero relations did not mean zero clinical links.
issues.implementation: Default outer step budget is 100 while case-level request/token budgets remain binding. Exhaustion now stops as max_steps, not max_turns. This changes a control bound, not candidate or relation semantics.

issues.problem: SCALE-01 relations-r2 returned a response whose 16 read_event calls were complete JSON objects but whose top-level list/envelope was unclosed. The parser discarded all 16, repeated the identical repair request, then stopped format_failed with no edges. It also issued a 16-call batch despite a protocol that encouraged smaller work units.
issues.implementation: Recover only fully decoded registered calls with object arguments from an unclosed envelope. Do not guess or execute a partial tail. Reply protocol now requests one tool per reply to keep production bounded; oversized batch guards remain. Recovered calls are marked in session.

issues.problem: SCALE-01 relations-r4 finally recorded ten valid edges but recovery sessions repeated the complete candidate-list and spill reads, spending the remaining attempts before useful continuation. Repeated source/unit metadata made the list unnecessarily large.
issues.implementation: Recovery now updates self.relations after each attempt and supplies durable endpoint/relation pairs to the next prompt. Candidate list drops duplicate discovery unit/source metadata while preserving origin identifiers and exact spans. No change to clinical relation semantics.

issues.problem: SCALE-01 relations-r5 completed with 39 edges, but source-level citations allowed an evidence relation to cite unrelated findings from the same report instead of the candidate evidence span; unverified candidate spans could also be organized. One supported evidence_used claimed chest CT pneumonia/effusion supported albumin supplementation without an actual endpoint match.

real_counterexample.observation: 引文属于同一报告但与白蛋白处置无直接关联，不能作为supported关系。

issues.implementation: Every supported/context_only/no_link relation must include each endpoint's exact full located span, including evidence objects' source spans. Both endpoints must have program-verified ACCEPTED or SOURCE_INDEXED status. Evidence projection for organization derives immutable source spans from original_texts.

issues.problem: A fresh cache could lose the first billed response because its parent directory did not exist.
The internal tool registry schema was sent directly instead of the chat-completions function schema.
Transport retried unparseable provider content and bypassed the agent's bounded format repair; truncated content must remain a failure.
Replies outside content.tool_calls were treated as completed answers, making unread units look like genuine zero-event units.
A transport timeout in one discovery unit aborted the case, leaving later units unrun and discarding the distinction between a failed unit and an empty unit.
issues.limitations: Continuing other units does not certify the failed unit or make a case complete. Its proposals remain partial and its stop is unfinished. This is not a clinical validation.

issues.problem: An oversized tool batch crossed the registry limit before execution. In r6 ordering it was truncated after 162 complete compare_clocks calls and an unfinished call, then one ordinary format repair also failed. Sending the raw assistant text plus an ordinary user repair is invalid for providers that require a tool result for every advertised tool call.
issues.limitations: Complete prefix calls are not executed and the unfinished call is not guessed. Recovery is one bounded model repair; this does not certify ordering or clinical reconstruction. The repaired code was not part of r6.

issues.problem: The evaluator marked an INCOMPLETE harness run comparable merely because three files existed, so partial counts and token savings could be misread as an effect comparison.
issues.limitations: Legacy frozen summaries with explicit failures=0 are labelled LEGACY_NO_FAILURES; this is not clinical validation.

issues.problem: r5/r6 isolated transport failures but did not recover the failed unit. A request_failed unit remained incomplete even when its earlier proposals survived. Ordering also aborted on its first transport failure.

real_counterexample.note: r6 demonstrates failed-unit preservation, not recovery. Its ordering format failure is covered separately by HAG-LIVE-006.

issues.limitations: A recovery uses a fresh session and the same shared case budget. Discovery retains earlier proposals; identical local_ids are revisions, not duplicate events. recovery.exhausted means no further recovery was possible because the attempt limit or shared budget was reached. This is not in r6's contract and does not establish clinical correctness.

issues.problem: Completed r7 exposed three ordering-layer defects: relation/demotion basis_quotes were stored without the promised source verification; read_event omitted time_verdict; and same_event was treated as a process merge even though its own explanation described duplicate proposals for one admission plan.

real_counterexample.observation: Two atomic admission-plan proposals and one combined proposal were labelled same_event but flattened into one process without retaining an explicit duplicate-candidate group.

issues.limitations: Program citation verification does not establish that the model's semantic relation is clinically true. event_groups retain duplicate candidates without deleting or rewriting them. duplicate_candidate_groups also preserves an identity link across separate process containers; only same_management_process merges process containers. Repeated ordering calls preserve prior records rather than silently erasing identity links. These repairs are not part of r7's contract.

issues.problem: r9 completed all three stages and recovered the failed discovery unit, but _unfinished counted transient request_failed attempts and incorrectly labelled the final run INCOMPLETE.
issues.limitations: A recovered unit may be complete only when its final record is answered. An exhausted or otherwise failed final recovery remains unfinished, and all attempts remain in stage_stop_history. This correction does not rewrite r9's frozen summary, prove clinical correctness, or make its new candidate graph a clinical Reference.

issues.problem: r9 discovery accepted action/time quotations from an adjacent clinical document under the admission-note unit, while ordering's event summary showed source_ids=[] because that field was never propagated.

real_counterexample.observation: The assigned unit contained one admission source; the proposed action/time citations belonged to the adjacent first-course source in another unit. Exact whole-case quote lookup accepted the misplaced proposal. All 25 event summaries had empty source_ids.

issues.limitations: The reading unit is retained only as discovery task provenance. Each candidate's one exact source span determines origin, origin unit and retrieval clock; an absent or unknown origin is explicit and never borrows the assigned source or clock. Event ids retain their compatibility name but use sorted origin source ids plus local revision id; they do not certify clinical event identity and are not stable across the r9 schema. Historical r9 ids remain unchanged. This prevents false source attribution, not wrong semantic content, duplication across reading tasks, or an incorrect candidate boundary.

issues.problem: r9 recorded same-process links merely because actions shared a ward round, then a pure transitive assembly produced a nine-event container without any case-level container review. It also treated a combined proposal as same_event with each atomic component.

real_counterexample.observation: The visible ordering explanations explicitly named different goals but used the same ward round as the merge rationale. Sixteen relations were recorded with no preview_episodes call; the old pipeline had no episodes agent session. Three same_event links included combined-versus-atomic proposals.

issues.limitations: preview is now a program prerequisite for normal episode finish, and no_link refutes only a direct process pair while preserving history and other paths. Neither mechanism verifies clinical semantics or prevents an agent from proposing an incorrect link. Combined-versus-atomic identity remains a pending semantic/object-model issue; no automatic contains/subaction relation has been implemented or validated.

issues.problem: r9 inconsistently omitted an imaging report when its selection record was not found, retained other imaging findings as historical management events, and recorded no evidence_comparison_previous relations even when a later decision explicitly cited a CT.

real_counterexample.observation: Ordering read some imaging findings but did not read their complete units or the later report explicitly cited by a subsequent decision. It used no evidence_comparison_previous relation; the old proposal schema lacked evidence-specific fields.

issues.limitations: The program now indexes every discovered performed-test candidate report group without asking the discovery LLM for a management question, deployment sentence or selection reason. Evidence objects cannot be same_event or same_management_process endpoints and are listed separately rather than as singleton episodes. An evidence_comparison_previous relation does not union processes. The finish coverage list is a declared review receipt, not proof that the source was actually read or clinically matched. Whether the agent will preserve and link the real r9 reports remains untested.

issues.problem: The new episode review initially kept recorded additions outside the builder's final relation view, and transport recovery did not carry additions into the next attempt's recorded-relation store.

real_counterexample.observation: The historical defect motivating the new stage was pure assembly without review. The additional final-view/recovery defects were found in synthetic counterexamples while implementing the stage; r9 did not run this new code.

issues.limitations: The test proves retention, recovery bounds and final graph bookkeeping on synthetic events. It does not prove correct clinical containers, source coverage or real-provider recovery behavior.

issues.problem: r9 events had null clock_basis because build_units retained the normalized value only in original_texts while pipeline._event read the absent unit-level field.

real_counterexample.observation: All candidate events lacked a top-level clock_basis even though sources carried a computed basis.

issues.limitations: The regression proves propagation of the already-computed basis for document and imaging units. It does not reinterpret a report time, certify visibility, or establish a clinical decision time.

issues.problem: r9 showed inconsistent candidate granularity and scope handling across records, including execution text framed as a new choice, routine management retained in some units but omitted in others, and a scope=no proposal remaining active.

real_counterexample.observation: Comparable ward-round actions were split or grouped inconsistently; execution wording supplied a management question without a documented choice moment; a scope=no proposal was not demoted.

issues.limitations: Discovery no longer assigns event granularity and no longer collects prechoice/postchoice evidence or time claims. Multiple expressions, including combined and component expressions, remain located candidates. scope=no is preserved as an explicit exclusion index and is not active downstream; it is not patient exclusion. Masking is a verified program projection, not a frozen blinding protocol; adjacent explanations/results and future text need separate policy. Execution/repeat semantics, routine-management consistency and contains/subaction/overlap organization remain open and require real-model discovery-only validation. No hard-coded drug/tube rule or automatic patient/episode exclusion was added.

issues.problem: Multiple diagnostic events can share one exact exam timestamp without a source-proven draft/revision relationship, and a placeholder-only report can otherwise be treated as substantive evidence. SCALE-06 has two events at 2022-10-02 19:49:19; EA-8eb24374e2c9b4d4 contains only original_findings/original_impression 已写 placeholders and has no evidence-arrival Checkpoint.

real_counterexample.observation: The two events have the same exam time and report times 23 seconds apart; the latter is placeholder-only. Same-time identity alone does not prove that the reports are the same clinical event or version.

issues.positive_control: Distinct events with a shared exam timestamp retain their IDs and source clocks while receiving an explicit review flag. Placeholder text is identified without deleting the source.
issues.negative_control: The program does not silently merge same-time events, infer draft/final versions, or claim that placeholder text is new patient evidence.
issues.limitations: Only an event whose resolved sources are all placeholders is blocked from an evidence-arrival candidate. A mixed event with substantive source text remains reviewable. Same-time events retain distinct IDs and are not clinically merged.

issues.problem: Management checkpoints could claim NEW_EVIDENCE_ROUND while their structured new-evidence state was empty, and a future management plan could be cited as patient evidence. SCALE-05 CP-M-de486fdafa1fb3fd1b85 used future routine examination plans as support.

real_counterexample.observation: The cited current member span described future examinations rather than an arrived result; four non-initial management checkpoints had empty structured new/input evidence.

issues.positive_control: A deterministic diagnostic event strictly after the comparator and no later than the current checkpoint is recorded separately from Agent citations and non-diagnostic source assertions.
issues.negative_control: An old diagnostic citation alone, a missing comparator, or an empty evidence interval produces REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than evidence evolution. A citation overlapping the current management-action span is rejected.
issues.limitations: The projection does not certify clinical truth or prove that the historical team actually used the evidence.

issues.problem: Pathology pre-acquisition and post-report checkpoints could share one report-time clock even when an earlier specimen time existed. Thirteen previous pre/post pairs shared a clock; ten had an earlier specimen time.

real_counterexample.observation: A missing exam_time caused the pre-acquisition evaluation to fall back to report_time, collapsing the evidence boundary.

issues.positive_control: For pathology only, a consistent earlier specimen_time anchors the pre-acquisition state when exam_time is unavailable.
issues.negative_control: CT/MR do not use specimen fallback. Report-time fallback or unresolved same-clock pre/post states receive DEGRADED_PRE_POST_SAME_CLOCK_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than a fabricated time interval.
issues.limitations: Specimen time is an evaluation proxy, not a confirmed historical choice time or report visibility time.

issues.problem: Twenty-one previous postoperative checkpoints retained preoperative phases/actions. SCALE-09 CP-D-07ca532b66d50ea61a75 labelled postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy as NAT.

real_counterexample.observation: Postoperative adjuvant treatment was represented as a preoperative NAT-phase task.

issues.positive_control: Non-routine postoperative candidates remain visible in a non-primary trajectory and retain original source actions for review.
issues.negative_control: Postoperative candidates do not merge into preoperative same-question checkpoints, are not primary P2 evaluation items, and preoperative action semantics trigger ACTION_TASK_MISMATCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED. Routine postoperative care remains outside the main task.
issues.limitations: The program does not rewrite START_NAT into a clinically confirmed adjuvant action; source labels and task mismatch remain explicit.

issues.problem: The action response needed explicit no-op and technical-abstention semantics, duplicate diagnostic actions required merged provenance, and unexported drafts needed material/form binding.

real_counterexample.observation: Two different diagnostic action_types targeted the same CT/MR action and duplicated the displayed candidate.

issues.positive_control: ACTIONS_PROPOSED requires at least one action; NO_NEW_ACTION and ABSTAIN export no actions; same-target diagnostic actions retain merged event/type provenance; valid submitted responses bind manifest and form version.
issues.negative_control: ABSTAIN is not a fourth clinical Mode; no-op cannot export an action; stale-key, stale-manifest and stale-form drafts are neither restored nor exported. The action dictionary is a draft, not a prefilled Reference.
issues.limitations: Clinical action availability, formal Q1-Q5 Reference and E/F/M/A/U scoring are not frozen or implemented by this engineering schema.

issues.problem: Adversarial review of the first r31 implementation found eight uncovered paths: placeholder events could still support management evidence evolution; supporting management spans escaped overlap checks; missing visibility raised NameError; independent same-time BEFORE events merged; no-op states exported evidence requests; pathology specimen clock handling diverged; postoperative diagnostic actions lacked mismatch review; and HTML trusted caller-supplied manifest identity without a form content hash.

real_counterexample.observation: The affected fresh SCALE-05 and SCALE-09 runs were stopped during Discovery after 41 and 36 successful provider invocations respectively. Their partial outputs are not complete validation results.

issues.positive_control: Substantive mixed-source events remain eligible, explicit joint diagnostic groups still merge, ACTIONS_PROPOSED still exports its action/evidence fields, and correctly canonicalized materials render with bound manifest/form hashes.
issues.negative_control: Placeholder-only evidence, supporting management plans, unjoined same-time events, missing/conflicting clocks, no-op evidence requests, postoperative preoperative-action semantics and stale/tampered response envelopes cannot silently pass their respective gates.
issues.limitations: The stopped r31 requests are retained only as execution receipts. Clinical correctness and fresh end-to-end behavior require the separate r32 run.

issues.problem: A fresh adjudication can record every required management CP and then return a prose summary without calling finish, leaving an otherwise complete result INCOMPLETE. The initial r32 command also used stages=case, which runs legacy case organization rather than trajectory adjudication.

real_counterexample.observation: All 12 management checkpoints were adjudicated, missing_checkpoint_ids and attempt_problems were empty and list coverage was complete, but stop was not_finished because Agent omitted the finish tool.

issues.positive_control: After Agent has answered, the program may perform the deterministic finish validation only when every management CP is adjudicated, no attempt problem exists, and every candidate CP was listed. The validation is recorded in final.program_completion_validation.
issues.negative_control: Missing adjudications still produce not_finished and no program completion validation. The fallback does not invent or alter any clinical adjudication.
issues.limitations: SCALE-05 legacy case organization was complete; SCALE-09 legacy case organization reached max_steps and is not claimed complete. Its fresh Discovery answered all 60 units, and subsequent trajectory validation uses that fresh Discovery rather than the unrelated legacy organization stage.

issues.problem: The trajectory projection inherited the admission-intent rule but its intent vocabulary omitted 进一步治疗. A fresh SCALE-05 admission sentence was therefore retained as the first management checkpoint even though the legacy projection excluded equivalent admission intent.

real_counterexample.quote: 今为进一步治疗来我院就诊，门诊以"胰腺肿瘤"收入院
real_counterexample.observation: Discovery proposed 住院评估/胰腺肿瘤 and adjudication retained FIRST_VISIBLE; the sentence states admission intent, not an independent actionable management choice.

issues.positive_control: Concrete diagnostic, treatment and reassessment actions remain candidates under the existing rules.
issues.negative_control: The exact further-treatment admission sentence becomes SUPPORT_ONLY/ADMISSION_INTENT_NOT_INDEPENDENT_DECISION in both projections and produces no independent checkpoint.
issues.limitations: Removing this checkpoint changes the provisional comparator chain; prior adjudication artifacts cannot simply be relabelled as valid for the corrected projection.

issues.problem: The postoperative action-mismatch guard treated any target containing 切除 as preoperative, including an explicitly postoperative recurrence reassessment.

real_counterexample.observation: The candidate action was reassessment/胰十二指肠切除术后术区复发可能性大 in POSTOPERATIVE_TRAJECTORY, but the word 切除 triggered ACTION_TASK_MISMATCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED.

issues.positive_control: START_NAT with 术后辅助化疗 and explicit preoperative resection/NAT semantics still receive mismatch review.
issues.negative_control: An explicitly postoperative recurrence reassessment does not receive a preoperative-action mismatch flag merely because the operation name contains 切除.
issues.limitations: This deterministic review-flag correction does not change checkpoint topology or adjudication and therefore does not require another model run.

issues.problem: SCALE-01 CP4 paired a postoperatively visible preoperative CT report with reassess-resectability. The program emitted ACTION_TASK_MISMATCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED but had no Agent review or downstream migration; merely clearing the flag would have preserved the wrong task. Standardized action phase mismatches could also bypass the old keyword-only trigger.

real_counterexample.observation: CT exam 2022-12-14 14:31, report visible 2022-12-15 15:55, operation started 2022-12-15 09:00; Discovery retained reassess-resectability although the report could not inform that completed operation.

issues.positive_control: After the dedicated context and complete current/operative sources are actually delivered, the case-level Agent may remove an independent diagnostic CP while conserving its report as context, or retain it with a phase-valid canonical action. Baseline management CP IDs and evidence-arrival grouping remain stable.
issues.negative_control: A spill preview, missing operation record, free-text replacement, management-CP deletion, phase-invalid action, forged operation provenance, or regrouped adjudication ID cannot pass. Old adjudications without action_reviews remain renderable.
issues.limitations: The 26-action dictionary is DRAFT_NOT_CLINICAL_REFERENCE and not a patient-specific acceptable-action set. Agent review is a candidate audit, not clinical confirmation. Both r49 SCALE-01 runs removed the postoperatively visible preoperative-CT independent CP and rendered 9 CPs with conserved migrations; the fresh run also standardized postoperative-pathology actions. OTHER_SPECIFIED still includes broad preoperative-assessment wording and needs further specificity review. SCALE-02/05/06/09 were not rerun in r49. HAR-LIVE-039 supersedes mandatory canonical actions and phase validation in subsequent versions.

issues.problem: The r49 action dictionary became an erroneous cognitive and structural gate: Discovery required action_id, rejected abstract or unlisted actions, action review required a phase-valid replacement, and downstream projections filtered null-action candidates out of independent CPs. A valid but unlisted management action such as patient-specific biliary drainage could therefore cause tool errors or distort candidate selection. Formal report time was also worded as actual result visibility although clinicians may review images earlier.

real_counterexample.observation: A CP must remain valid with no reference action or with OTHER_SPECIFIED free text such as endoscopic biliary stent drainage; report time is a documentation proxy, not the clinician's actual image-review time.

issues.positive_control: Discovery accepts new_decision/reassessment and diagnostic yes with null action; downstream projections retain those management and diagnostic CPs with an empty action list while repeat/execution remain support; OTHER_SPECIFIED preserves free action_type/target; retained CP review accepts null or unlisted actions without action-phase rejection. Report-time wording explicitly permits earlier clinician image review.
issues.negative_control: Source/span verification, mandatory current and operative source reading for phase-conflict review, management-CP deletion prohibition, migration conservation, and evidence-evolution guards remain enforced.
issues.limitations: The fresh r50 SCALE-01 run completed all 38 Discovery units with no action/tool errors, accepted null and free-text actions, and rendered 10 CPs with conserved migrations. Reference actions remain optional LLM annotations, not a complete or clinically validated action set and not blind-review answers. HAR-LIVE-040 separately records the null-action time-review bypass found in this run.

issues.problem: The first r50 fresh run accepted null diagnostic actions but thereby bypassed the action-dependent postoperative conflict flag. CP-D-9b20fc3898f377a385b5 represented a CT acquired before the recorded operation but reported afterward, yet remained an independent CP without review. A time-order guard must not depend on an optional action annotation.

real_counterexample.observation: CT exam_time 2022-12-14 14:31:11 preceded operation_start 2022-12-15 09:00, while report_time 2022-12-15 15:55:12 followed it. The after-arrival Discovery action was null and r50 provisionally retained the CP without action review.

issues.positive_control: An after-arrival CP whose precise exam time precedes the operation and whose report proxy follows it receives ACTION_TASK_MISMATCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED even when candidate_action is null. The review context supplies acquisition clocks and does not require an action.
issues.negative_control: A CT both acquired and reported after the operation receives no acquisition/report inversion flag; coarse same-day clocks do not assert an order. Optional open actions, source reading, span checks and migration conservation remain unchanged.
issues.limitations: The fresh r51 SCALE-01 run completed all 38 Discovery units and checkpoint adjudication with no tool errors. The Agent read the full CT and operation sources, removed CP-D-9b20fc3898f377a385b5 as an independent CP while retaining the report as context, and rendered 9 CPs with conserved migrations. The flag requests candidate review; it neither proves the clinician's actual image-review time nor automatically deletes a CP. The historical flag name is retained for interface compatibility although the trigger no longer requires an action.

issues.problem: Optional open actions and acquisition/report/operation conflict review needed multi-case fresh-run stability evidence rather than a single SCALE-01 result or frozen-Discovery replay.

real_counterexample.observation: All five fresh runs completed 314 Discovery units and adjudication with 1665 requests and 20337892 tokens, no unfinished units, transport recoveries or adjudication attempt problems, and conserved management/diagnostic migrations. The five previews contain 9, 17, 19, 6 and 15 CPs respectively (66 total); 215 null-action submissions were accepted without action gate errors.

issues.positive_control: SCALE-01 and SCALE-06 each required review of a preoperatively acquired but postoperatively reported diagnostic source even with an empty reference action; the Agent read the diagnostic and operative originals, removed independent CP status and conserved the report as context. SCALE-09 retained an after-arrival contrast-CT CP with no reference action.
issues.negative_control: No optional-action or action-phase gate was restored. Source/span verification, evidence evolution review, complete current and operative source reading for time-conflict review, and migration conservation remained active.
issues.limitations: This is engineering and candidate-topology stability evidence, not clinical accuracy validation or an expert Reference. SCALE-05 retained 19 CPs versus 15 in the older frozen-Discovery r48 projection: six management CPs are REVIEW_REQUIRED/UNCERTAIN, comprising four same-clock documents, one unclear evidence-time relation and one evidence-quote overlap. Conservative same-clock retention still creates visible redundancy and is not resolved. The 11-09 cancellation/biopsy CP was not supported by the future CT report. Old r48 CP counts are structural references only, not matched fresh-run cost comparisons. Formal report time remains a documentation proxy, not actual clinician image-review time.

issues.problem: In fresh r52 SCALE-05, four management documents on 2023-11-08 shared the same 08:23 laboratory evidence round and surgical plan. The Agent initially submitted RETAIN_CP+NEW_EVIDENCE_ROUND for two of them, but any same-clock peer forced REVIEW_REQUIRED+UNCERTAIN. Review checkpoints then remained independent in materials but were excluded from later comparators, so all four repeatedly compared with 11-07 and no semantic same-round merge was possible. The context also lacked a same-clock landscape and did not require management-comparator original reading.

real_counterexample.observation: Two RETAIN submissions were rejected by UNORDERED_CANDIDATE_STATE_REQUIRES_REVIEW; the accepted REVIEW results all cited the same red-cell report and retained four independent candidates. Same-clock ordering cannot be inferred, but same-clock semantic support does not require an ordering claim.

issues.positive_control: A same-clock retained or review CP can be the automatic comparator for SUPPORT_ONLY; a later CP also sees a strictly earlier REVIEW CP. The context exposes all same-clock candidate/source indexes and the current plus management-comparator originals must be fully delivered. Offline projection conserves same-clock SUPPORT migrations independent of adjudication item order and mixed-precision clock representation.
issues.negative_control: Unknown-clock and multiple-parallel-state ambiguity still requires review; FIRST_VISIBLE cannot be repeated after a same-clock retained/review state. A same-clock SUPPORT cannot bypass timed original reports after the strictly earlier baseline, and new evidence still requires strict comparator-to-report ordering, original citation and span checks.
issues.limitations: Adversarial audits and submission-path review found and this change closes six additional paths: baseline-new-report bypass through a same-clock comparator, disposition leakage across offline items, online/offline mixed-precision disagreement, misclassifying a same-clock diagnostic comparator's existing target as new, misclassifying a same-clock management comparator's cited laboratory batch as new, and hiding a later laboratory result through broad batch exclusion. Full harness tests are 492 passed with 87 subtests and default tests are 171 passed. Fresh r54 full Discovery plus adjudication completed for SCALE-05 and SCALE-09 with 374 and 368 real model requests, zero transport recoveries, complete adjudication and conserved migration. In SCALE-05, fresh Discovery consolidated three of the four former same-clock candidates into CP-M-696a5083115a6941f4b4 and global adjudication merged CP-M-e2dd7ea92330b0769281 as SAME_ROUND_SUPPORT; the Agent had fully read both the receiving and current management originals before submission. Material CP count changed from 19 to 16. In SCALE-09, eight management candidates were merged as support and material CP count changed from 15 to 16 because fresh Discovery also changed the candidate/diagnostic topology; counts are not a controlled paired effectiveness measure. SCALE-05 still retains one REVIEW_REQUIRED CP for CT report-time versus earlier clinical-restatement uncertainty. Semantic acceptance is not expert confirmation or clinical accuracy validation.

issues.problem: New evidence alone was previously sufficient to retain a management checkpoint. Repeated plans or execution notes could therefore become independent CPs despite no substantive reassessment. During the first fresh SCALE-05 validation, a repeated external-MRI quote with incorrect manual offsets also caused 59 identical rejected submissions and exhausted the 100-step adjudication budget.

real_counterexample.observation: Fresh full-pipeline runs identified new laboratory or imaging evidence in documents that only repeated established plans. The first SCALE-05 r55 run remained INCOMPLETE and is retained as a failure receipt; after unique-context quote guidance, fresh r56 completed without adjudication attempt problems.

issues.positive_control: RETAIN_CP+NEW_EVIDENCE_ROUND requires both new evidence and substantive reassessment. CONTEXT_ONLY+NEW_EVIDENCE_ROUND advances the evidence timeline without creating an independent CP. A later substantive reassessment can carry continuous or same-clock context evidence using original source IDs; external or unclear-source evidence retains specific review tags. Offline projection reconnects the next independent CP to the last retained comparator without backfilling later evidence.
issues.negative_control: SUPPORT_ONLY still requires no new evidence. Invalid CONTEXT_ONLY evolution, empty evidence, reused same-hash copies, false source promotion, and disconnected or backfilled projections fail. Error guidance rejects repeated quotes with manual offsets and directs the Agent to search or read a larger unique quote.
issues.limitations: Complete fresh SCALE-05 r56 used 369 requests and SCALE-09 r55 used 358 requests; they rendered 12 and 15 candidate CPs with conserved migrations and no empty visible context. Two and four management adjudications respectively became CONTEXT_ONLY; all 27 rendered CPs passed browser traversal. These are uncontrolled fresh runs, not paired clinical-effectiveness measurements. SCALE-05 retains one REVIEW_REQUIRED management CP for source/time uncertainty and one empty-new-evidence-state review flag. SCALE-09 requires clinical review of the inference that worsening liver tests did not substantively affect a document repeating no contraindication to surgery. Candidate topology and Agent rationale are not expert Reference or clinical accuracy validation. The incomplete r55 SCALE-05 run is not included in the preview.
